entries.description: 技术架构设计规范(全栈):模块/系统怎么搭这一层——分层与依赖方向(依赖倒置·禁循环)、模块边界(按业务域纵切)、关注点分离、配置与密钥外置、无状态可扩展、契约先行;后端分层职责、单体优先与微服务拆分时机、服务间通信(REST·异步消息·ESB)、跨切面(鉴权·缓存·事务边界·幂等·异步任务);前端组件分层、目录模块、状态管理、API 封装、与后端契约对齐、前后端职责边界。设计新系统/模块/服务、划分结构、技术选型时(含 AI 辅助)遵循。Use when 设计架构、划分模块与目录结构、定分层与依赖方向、拆分服务或判断要不要拆微服务、设计服务间通信、放置鉴权/缓存/事务/幂等等跨切面、组织前端组件分层与状态管理、封装 API 客户端、对齐前后端契约。管层间/模块间/服务间结构,单个类/函数写法看 backend-code-style-spec。仅约束新增/改动,存量不追溯。

entries.name: backend-code-style-spec
entries.description: 后端代码风格与约定规范(命名/函数/错误处理/分层/注释/null),用于生成与编写符合团队要求的新后端代码。Use when 编写/生成/评审后端代码、命名变量与函数、组织分层(controller/service/repository)、处理业务错误与异常(抛 BizException 转 R<T>)、写注释、处理 null/空值时。新增或改动代码以本规范为准,不为贴合存量风格而偏离;机械格式交给 formatter/linter。涵盖 Java/Spring、Go、Node(TS)、Python 后端;前端组件级写法看 frontend-code-style-spec。

entries.name: cds-design
entries.description: 按 CDS（company-design-system）设计规范写新的前端页面或组件。当用户要求「做一个列表页/详情页/表单页」「加一个筛选栏」「实现这个组件」「按设计规范做界面」，或提到 CDS / 设计系统 / 组件库 / token 换肤时使用。产出符合规范的骨架 + 边写边跑门禁 + 模糊点登记而非臆造。

entries.name: cds-release
entries.description: CDS（company-design-system，仓库 company-design）发布 @company/cds / @company/cds-react / @company/cds-vue 三包时使用。覆盖发版前校验、版本号五处一致、CHANGELOG、MR 合 main、push nexus 触发 Jenkins、回读验证，以及发布失败的逐条对号入座。凡要「发版/发布 CDS」「升版本号」「触发 Jenkins 发布」「nexus 分支」「npm 私服 3.0.x」时使用。

entries.name: cds-review
entries.description: 对现有前端代码做 CDS（company-design-system）设计规范体检。当用户要求「检查 UI 是否符合规范」「做设计规范体检」「审查前端样式合规性」「看看这个页面有没有违反设计系统」，或提到 CDS / 设计规范 / token 合规 / 对比度审计 / 无障碍检查时使用。产出分档结论 + 按优先级排序的缺陷清单 + 明确的未覆盖声明。

entries.name: contract-esign-e2e
entries.description: 在 OA 测试环境对合同类审批流程（销售合同 / 无收支合同 / 无收支合同（有模板）/ 采购合同·快速审批 / 采购合同·新 / 资金往来合同，共 6 条）的电子签能力做端到端回归，覆盖发起、审批链、印章保管人确认、我方盖章、对方签署、归档与缺陷复验。Use when 用户要求跑或续跑 contract-esign E2E、合同电子签回归、验证 OA 电子签缺陷，或提到 XSHT/WSZHTKS/EST/法大大测试链路。

entries.name: db-design-spec
entries.description: MySQL 数据库设计规范:表/列命名(单数 snake_case)、主键(雪花 BIGINT)、审计字段(create_by/create_time/del_flag)、字段类型(金额 DECIMAL/时间 DATETIME/枚举 VARCHAR 常量)、索引、软删除、迁移。建表或改表时(含 AI 辅助编码)必须遵循。Use when 建表/改表、写 DDL/CREATE TABLE、定义数据库实体或表结构、设计字段类型与索引、写数据库迁移、命名表和列、设计主键与审计字段。仅约束新增/改动的表，存量不追溯。

entries.name: deploy-platform

entries.name: diagnose-windows-sandbox-acl
entries.description: Use on Windows for unexpected DSH sandbox access denials: workspace writes or listing fail, or an ordinarily readable path cannot be read. One bundled command inspects the path and every ancestor and repairs the ACL problems it proves in that same run. Expected confinement denials need no ACL repair.

entries.name: esb-apikey-invoke
entries.description: 无法签名的上游用 API Key（HMAC 降级档）接入企业服务总线(ESB) POST /api/esb/invoke-apikey（仅内网），生成调用代码并答疑。Use when 上游签不了 HMAC、要用 X-Api-Key 调 /api/esb/invoke-apikey、生成 apikey 调用代码、或问 ESB apikey 档的时间窗/nonce/flow 白名单/403/429/错误码。能签名的上游改用 esb-hmac-invoke。

entries.name: frontend-code-style-spec
entries.description: 前端代码风格与约定规范(React+Vue,TS):组件级写法——组件与文件命名、props 与事件定型(不 any/不改 props)、组件职责与拆分、状态与不可变(不直接 mutate、可派生不入 state)、副作用清理与依赖、列表稳定 key(不用下标)、样式作用域隔离与设计变量(禁行内魔法值)、可访问性(语义标签/alt/label/键盘)、国际化(禁硬编码用户可见文案)、空/加载/错误三态、注释。编写或改动前端组件时(含 AI 辅助)遵循。Use when 写 React/Vue 组件、定义 props 与事件、写 hooks 或 composable、管组件内状态与副作用、渲染列表、写组件样式、处理可访问性与 i18n、处理加载空错误态时。本文只管组件级写法:TS 语言约定看 backend-code-style-spec §2.3、前端结构分层看 architecture-design-spec §3。仅约束新增/改动,存量不追溯。服务端渲染(Go模板/htmx)+原生JS/CSS 项目先按规范内「适用栈判定」读——§1 适用、§2 不适用。

entries.name: git-workflow-spec
entries.description: 规范 AI 操作 git 的行为:提交/分支/推送/破坏性操作的红线与约定。执行任何 git 操作时遵循。Use when 提交代码(commit)、写 commit message、创建/命名分支、推送(push)、开 PR/MR、执行 reset/rebase/force push/clean 等操作时。核心红线:只在用户明确指令时才动 git、不 force push、不盲目 git add、不提交敏感信息、破坏性操作先确认;commit 用 Conventional(前缀英文+中文描述);特性分支+命名约定,禁直接改 main。

tools.name: mcp__pencil__browser
tools.description:
Interact with a real website loaded in the app's integrated browser: open a URL, reproduce a page (or one element) as editable canvas layers, screenshot it, or pull its DOM/screenshot back into the conversation.

Use it to iterate on real designs: import a live page onto the canvas, take inspiration from a site, or close the loop when generating a design — load the generated page, look at it, and refine.

Parameters:
- action (required):
  - "load-page": load "url" in the target browser (opening the sidebar if closed and no "nodeId" is given). Returns when the load finishes or fails.
  - "import-to-canvas": reproduce the target as editable Pencil layers on the canvas. The response reports the imported top-level frame's id for use with the execute tool. Each imported node's "context" field holds the source element's tag, prefixed with its code component name when detected (e.g. "Card - div") — useful for locating the element in the code.
  - "screenshot-to-canvas": place a screenshot of the target on the canvas as an image.
  - "return-element": return the target element's DOM and computed styles as text so you can read/reuse it.
  - "return-screenshot": return a screenshot of the target as an image so you can look at it.
  - "cdp": send one Chrome DevTools Protocol command ("method" + "params") to the target page and return its result as JSON text (a "Page.captureScreenshot" result comes back as an image). Use it to act inside the page: click, type, scroll, navigate.
- nodeId: for a canvas browser, pass its node id on every call, including CDP, captures, and reloads. Find the id in get_app_state or with execute. Omit nodeId to use the browser sidebar.
- target (default "full-page"): what to act on.
  - "full-page": the whole page.
  - "selection": the element the user picked with the browser's element picker (errors if none).
  - "query": the element resolved from "querySelector".
- querySelector: a CSS selector, required when target is "query".
- url: an http(s) or file URL, required (and only used) when action is "load-page".
- method: the CDP method, e.g. "Input.dispatchMouseEvent". Required (and only used) when action is "cdp".
- params: the CDP command's parameters, e.g. {"expression": "document.title", "returnByValue": true} for Runtime.evaluate. Used only when action is "cdp".

Usage:
- Call action "load-page" before the other actions so a page is loaded and visible.
- localhost dev servers usually live-reload: when the page is already loaded, skip "load-page" and check the result directly (e.g. "return-screenshot"); only if your change is not visible, reload with "load-page" and check again.
- Prefer target "query" or "selection" over "full-page" to keep imports and reads focused.
- Be careful with "return-element" on "body"/"html" or broad selectors: a whole page's DOM can be huge and overflow the context. Query a specific section (e.g. "header", ".pricing", "#hero"), or use "return-screenshot" to view the whole page cheaply.
- "return-screenshot" is for you to inspect visually; "screenshot-to-canvas" and "import-to-canvas" put the result in the user's document.
- Imported pages land as normal canvas nodes. Do NOT think in CSS/HTML afterwards — treat the result as a design and edit it with the execute tool like any other content.

Using CDP
- A command that starts a navigation (including a click on a link) returns once the load finishes.
- Only the DOM, Input, Page, Runtime, Emulation, CSS and Accessibility domains are available.
- Do not send Escape: the editor intercepts it and deselects the node.
- Check the result with "return-screenshot" or "return-element".

Examples:
- Reproduce a hero section as editable layers: {action: "load-page", url: "https://example.com"}, then {action: "import-to-canvas", target: "query", querySelector: "header.hero"}.
- Rebuild a component faithfully: {action: "return-element", target: "query", querySelector: ".pricing-card"} to read its DOM and styles, then {action: "return-screenshot", target: "query", querySelector: ".pricing-card"} to check your own render against it.
- Check a locally served page in its canvas preview: {action: "cdp", nodeId: "<preview node id>", method: "Runtime.evaluate", params: {expression: "document.title", returnByValue: true}}, then {action: "return-screenshot", nodeId: "<preview node id>", target: "full-page"}. Substitute the same actual node id in both calls.
- Open a menu inside the page: locate "button.menu" with DOM.querySelector and DOM.getBoxModel, click its centre with Input.dispatchMouseEvent, then {action: "return-screenshot"}.

action.description: What to do: load-page, import-to-canvas, screenshot-to-canvas, return-element, return-screenshot, or cdp.

method.description: A Chrome DevTools Protocol method, e.g. "Input.dispatchMouseEvent". Required when action is "cdp".

nodeId.description: Id of a browser node in the document to drive. Omit to drive the browser sidebar's own page.

params.description: The CDP command's parameters for "method", e.g. {"expression": "document.title", "returnByValue": true} for Runtime.evaluate. Used when action is "cdp".

querySelector.description: A CSS selector executed in the page. Required when target is "query".

uri.description: The URI of the .pen document (for example file:///path/to/design.pen).

url.description: An http(s) or file URL to load. Used when action is "load-page".

edits.description: When an execute call fails, ALWAYS retry with this instead of resending the snippet in `input`. Each edit replaces `find` with `replace` in the failed snippet, then the patched snippet re-runs from scratch. Edits apply in order: each `find` must match the snippet as already modified by the preceding edits. Requires `editId`; omit `input` when using it. If the patched snippet fails again, keep fixing it with further `edits` under the same editId - `find` must then match the already-patched snippet.

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

find.description: Exact text in the failed snippet to replace. Must match exactly once unless `all` is true.

input.description: The JavaScript snippet to execute. Required unless `edits` is provided.

uri.description: The URI of the .pen document (for example file:///path/to/design.pen).

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

rrule.description: Supported RFC 5545 subset: one DTSTART line, a newline, and one RRULE line. DTSTART ends in Z for UTC or carries TZID with an IANA time zone; a fixed offset such as UTC+5 is Etc/GMT-5, with the sign reversed. DTSTART must name an existing local time. A TZID rule keeps local clock time across daylight-saving changes; generated nonexistent local times are skipped, and repeated ones occur once, at the earlier instant. DTSTART may be in the past; delivery starts with the first occurrence after creation. A one-time delivery is RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1. No SECONDLY; BYSECOND takes one value. COUNT is at most 1000; use UNTIL for longer rules. MINUTELY and HOURLY accept no BY parts, so select clock times with DAILY or WEEKLY plus BYHOUR and BYMINUTE. BYMONTHDAY and ordinal BYDAY require MONTHLY or YEARLY; BYYEARDAY and BYWEEKNO require YEARLY. Ordinal BYDAY cannot combine with BYWEEKNO. Each FREQ period allows at most 10080 candidates before BYSETPOS, which accepts at most 31 values. UNTIL is a UTC instant ending in Z. Example: "DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Singapore:20260901T080000\nRRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1"

tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.
